- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
EMQX isn't the cause. The chat fails on a broken Cozo query in the bridge that's running now, before EMQX is ever touched.

**What fails:** `chat_response.start_conversation` (log `/var/log/op-dbus/op-grpc-bridge-release/current`, op `bdc201a4…`, `failure_kind="unclassified_backend_failure"`). All 27 calls today failed the same way. None appear in older logs, so your UI refactor is the first thing to call this method. The code has been broken since Oct 3 and nothing exercised it until now.

**Root cause:** `count_principal_conversations` in `crates/op-cozo-store/src/chat_response_conversations.rs` is the conversation-quota check that runs before anything is written. In the deployed binary (`/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/op-grpc-bridge`, built Oct 23) it runs:
```
?[cnt] := chat_conversation{principal_id: $principal_id, _}, cnt :=count
```
The relation `chat_conversation` doesn't exist (it's `chat_response_conversations`). The query also uses `$principal_id`, but `principal_params` only binds `$principal`. Cozo rejects it on every call. I confirmed that string is inside the deployed binary. The bug came in with commit `030752c`.

**Why EMQX is ruled out:** in `chat_response_state.rs`, the EMQX doorbell is fire-and-forget and only rings after a commit. Nothing was ever committed: `/dev/shm/opdbus/ui-workspaces/chat-responses/` has no per-owner directory.

**Status of the fix:**
- **Your uncommitted working tree already fixes the query** (`count(conversation_id)` over `*chat_response_conversations`, with `$principal`).
- **That fix isn't in any binary.** `target/release/op-grpc-bridge` was built at 16:41 and the fix was saved at 16:49, so that binary still has the broken query. Nothing has been deployed.

**A second problem will appear once you deploy the fix:** the same working-tree change adds `vectorized_at` and `cleared_at` columns to `chat_response_turns`. The live DB at `/var/lib/op-dbus/chat-responses.db` was created at 12:23 by the old binary, with the old columns.
- `initialize_chat_response_store` ignores the "already exists" error from `:create`.
- The startup check that follows then asks for the new columns and fails.
- So every `chat_response` method will still fail, with a different error.

You need one of these:
1. **Reset that DB.** It should be empty, since no conversation was ever started, but I'd confirm that before deleting it.
2. **Add a migration** that adds the two columns when the relation already exists.

**Smaller issue:** a quota or validation failure at this step happens before anything is written, but it's reported as "outcome unknown / do not retry". That's because `before_effect_refusal` doesn't classify it. The message overstates the risk, and the real error text is hidden from the log.

Do you want me to add the migration (or reset the empty DB) and then run the build and `./activate-golden.sh`?

The socket is attached to the chatbot container, but that container is stopped and failing to boot. `3tched-container` doesn't have it at all.

**"Lungs"** is the project's name for the per-identity D-Bus socket. AGENTS.md describes 3tchedFS as the container's "lungs." The host bridge (`op-grpc-bridge`, pid 2110) listens on `/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock` and admits every call through it under that container's identity (`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/lungs_socket.rs`). It's how an identity container reaches op-dbus without leaving its own permissions.

| Container | Lungs socket | State |
|---|---|---|
| `3tchedCtlChatbot` | Yes, through the `3tched-lungs` profile (host `/run/opdbus/lungs` mounted read-only at the same path) | **STOPPED**: last start (Oct 26 18:07) failed with `Failed to exec "/sbin/init"` |
| `3tched-container` | **No.** It only uses the `default` profile and has just a root disk | Running |
| `qdrant-recovered` | Not relevant (it only has its own Qdrant socket proxies) | Running |

The host side is fine: the socket exists and the bridge is listening on it.

**What this means for chat:** even after the Cozo fix, whatever is meant to answer turns from inside `3tchedCtlChatbot` can't, because the container can't boot. Its root filesystem in the `identity-roots` pool has no `/sbin/init`. That points to an empty or wrongly mounted leaf or seed, which fits the storage restoration work. The bridge's in-process control-plane chatbot doesn't depend on that container. Which one your EMQX refactor sends turns to decides whether this matters for the error you saw.

**One mismatch I noticed:** `crates/op-chat/src/system_prompt.rs:247` tells the model the socket is at `/run/3tched-lungs.socket`. The container actually mounts it at `/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock`. A model inside the container would look in the wrong place.


- **Expected:** under the identity storage design, start is supposed to have the host mount owner mount this identity's existing pair here: the shared read-only seed plus the identity's own writable leaf.
- **What happened:** that didn't occur on the Oct 26 18:07 start. LXC tried to run `/sbin/init` from the empty placeholder and aborted.

**Where things stand:**

| Mount | Status |
|---|---|
| Lungs socket (Incus disk device through the `3tched-lungs` profile) | ✅ attached, and the bridge is listening on the host |
| Container root (seed + leaf, mounted by the host mount owner) | ❌ not mounted, so the container can't boot |
| `3tched-container` | Has no lungs device at all. It isn't on the `3tched-lungs` profile |

I haven't changed anything. The storage rules say start may only verify and remount the existing pair through the host mount owner, never add or remove Btrfs members or fall back to anything else. So the next step is to find out why that mount owner didn't mount the pair: whether it's missing, whether it ran and failed, or whether the leaf is absent after the restoration.

# Incus: configuration first, storage-driver ownership

Project-local skill authored from the official Incus documentation below;
not an imported third-party skill or a container-sandbox wrapper. Documentation
review is not proof that any example has been applied to this host. Check the
installed client/server version and applicable API extensions before using
version-dependent options.

## Start with the actual declaration

An Incus instance is configured through instance properties, `config`,
`devices` and ordered `profiles`. The CLI exposes this as YAML; do not invent
a separate authoritative YAML file on disk. Incus owns its configuration.

Read both local and expanded instance configuration. Later profiles override
earlier ones; instance-local configuration overrides profiles. Editing a
shared profile affects every instance that uses it. Do not use expanded
configuration as a blind replacement: it flattens inherited settings.

Read-only infrastructure diagnostics, within the assigned maintenance scope:

```sh
incus version
incus config show <instance>
incus config show <instance> --expanded
incus profile show <profile>
incus storage show <pool>
incus storage volume list <pool>
incus storage volume show <pool> container/<instance>
```

Confirm the selected remote, project, instance type, native UUID and stopped
or running state. A name alone is not an identity or authorization proof.
Use `--force-local` only when explicitly diagnosing this host's local daemon.

## Declare native disks under devices

Example fragment for a NEW container's root on an existing Btrfs pool named

content.text:
The lungs mount is now on the template container. A test call through it from inside the template was refused with `Access denied`, which is what should happen at this stage.

**What I changed:** I added one Incus disk device to `3tched-container`, with the same settings the chatbot's `3tched-lungs` profile uses:
```
lungs-socket-dir: type=disk  source=/run/opdbus/lungs  path=/run/opdbus/lungs  readonly=true
```
It's still the one shared host socket. It's mounted read-only inside the container. I didn't add the profile's `/run` tmpfs, because it would have covered the running template's own `/run`. To undo: `sudo incus config device remove 3tched-container lungs-socket-dir`.

**What happened when I tried it:**
- `lungs.sock` is visible inside the template.
- I called `BindCurrentContainer` through it with `busctl`, and the bridge answered `Call failed: Access denied`. The bridge log shows the connection and then its close.
- That's correct behaviour. The bridge only binds a caller whose process belongs to exactly one running, committed identity container, and the template has no identity (no session ID, no Cozo binding). The socket is reachable, but the template can't act through it.

**Still open:**
1. **The new device may not reach new identities.** The creation code in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/incus.rs:1490` builds the device list itself (`root` on `identity-roots`, `runtime-run`, …) rather than copying the template's devices. Whether new identities get the lungs mount depends on that code or the `3tched-lungs` profile, not on this template device. If the template is meant to be the source, that code needs changing.
2. **The chatbot still can't boot.** Its provision plan says the root should come from:
   - its leaf `/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/3tched-pool/3tchedCtlChatbot.img`, mounted at `.../3tched-pool/.mounts/3tchedCtlChatbot/root`
   - paired with the seed on `/dev/loop1p1`

   Neither is mounted right now; `losetup` shows only `loop0` (`3tched.img`). Its native rootfs is still an empty placeholder.

Should I check whether the leaf image exists and trace why the host mount owner didn't bring up the seed and leaf? I'd only read and inspect.

#!/bin/sh
# Host storage owner: remount/receive existing GPT members, never mint/start.
set -eu
fail() { printf 'restore-chatbot-root: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
check_only=false
if [ "${1:-}" = --check ]; then check_only=true; shift; fi
[ "$#" -le 1 ] || fail 'usage: restore-chatbot-root [--check] [NAME]'
name=${1:-3tchedCtlChatbot}
printf '%s' "$name" | grep -Eq '^(3tchedCtlChatbot|3tchedChatbot|ID-[1-9][0-9]*)$' && [ "${#name}" -le 63 ] || fail 'invalid chatbot selector'
# The name selects the native target; the same existing UUID/session/key and
# storage receipts below are required for both the legacy alias and ID-N.
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host root required'
sid=b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28
key=Env5zPMmM1Zhypu5/DY/yU4PRYW/4AOEq2KZ4OSc+18=
pool=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/3tched-pool
receipt=$pool/.provisioning/$name.boot.json
binding=$pool/.provisioning/$name.incus.json
disk=$pool/.provisioning/$name.json
root=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/$name/rootfs
view=$pool/.mounts/$name/root-view
seed_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/seed-layer
upgrade_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade-layer
readback() { timeout --kill-after=5s 30s "$@"; }
secure_path() (
    path=$1
    [ "$(realpath -e -- "$path")" = "$path" ] || fail "noncanonical path: $path"
    while :; do
        [ ! -L "$path" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u -- "$path")" = 0 ] &&
            [ $((0$(stat -c %a -- "$path") & 022)) -eq 0 ] || fail "unsafe owner/mode: $path"
        [ "$path" != / ] || break
        path=$(dirname -- "$path")
    done
)
secure_path "$pool"
[ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$pool")" = 0:0 ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o UUID)" = a1ab7b42-12a8-437c-8f65-d0469892c8dd ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M / -o UUID)" != a1ab7b42-12a8-437c-8f65-d0469892c8dd ] ||
    fail 'canonical loop pool is not mounted on its pinned filesystem'
secure_path "$pool/.provisioning"
[ -d "$pool/.provisioning" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$pool/.provisioning")" = 0:0:700 ] ||
    fail 'preparation receipt directory must be private'
for file in "$receipt" "$binding" "$disk"; do
    secure_path "$file"
    [ -f "$file" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$file")" = 0:0:600 ] || fail "unsafe preparation receipt: $file"
done
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$sid" '
    .version==1 and .name==$name and .session_id==$sid and
    .identity_registered==true and .restore_existing_pair==true
' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'chatbot boot attestation differs'
# The boot opt-in is not identity authority. Match the host preparation's
# existing native UUID/session/key and storage paths before any mount action.
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$sid" --arg key "$key" --arg root "$root" --arg view "$view" '
    .version==1 and .name==$name and .session_id==$sid and .phase=="root-bound" and
    .root_bound==true and .root_view_readonly==true and .upgrade_paired==true and
    .threetched_root==$root and .root_view==$view and .instance.name==$name and .instance.type=="container" and
    .instance.config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid and .instance.config["user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key"]==$key and
    (.instance.config["volatile.uuid"]|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$"))
' "$binding" >/dev/null || fail 'chatbot preparation pins differ'
uuid=$(jq -er '.instance.config["volatile.uuid"]' "$binding")
jq -e --arg uuid "$uuid" '
    (has("instance_uuid")|not) or .instance_uuid==$uuid
' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'boot native UUID differs'
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg image "$pool/$name.img" --arg root "$pool/.mounts/$name/root" \
    --arg upgrade "$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade" '
    .name==$name and .layout=="raw-gpt-root-upgrade-v1" and .phase=="filesystems-prepared" and
    .filesystem_prepared==true and .image==$image and .root_mount==$root and .upgrade_mount==$upgrade
' "$disk" >/dev/null || fail 'disk preparation pins differ'
image=$pool/$name.img
secure_path "$image"
[ -f "$image" ] && [ "$(stat -c %i "$image")" = "$(jq -r .image_inode "$disk")" ] &&
    [ "$(stat -c %s "$image")" = "$(jq -r .image_bytes "$disk")" ] || fail 'image pins differ'
instance=$(readback incus --force-local query "/1.0/instances/$name?project=default") || fail 'native instance readback failed'
printf '%s\n' "$instance" | jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$sid" --arg key "$key" --arg uuid "$uuid" '
    .name==$name and .type=="container" and .config["volatile.uuid"]==$uuid and
    .config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid and .config["user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key"]==$key and
    .config["security.privileged"]=="false" and .config["security.protection.shift"]=="true" and
    .config["boot.autostart"]=="false" and .profiles==["3tched-lungs"] and
    .devices.root.type=="disk" and .devices.root.path=="/" and .devices.root.pool=="identity-roots" and
    ((.status=="Stopped" and .status_code==102) or (.status=="Running" and .status_code==103))
' >/dev/null || fail 'native chatbot UUID/session/key/policy differs'
state=$(printf '%s\n' "$instance" | jq -er .status)
# Select the activated closure deliberately. When invoked from a source or
# received release, use that helper's sibling; never fall through to base copies.
self=$(realpath -e -- "$0") || fail 'cannot resolve restore helper'
helper_dir=$(dirname -- "$self")
case "$helper_dir" in
    /usr/local/libexec/3tched)
        helper_dir=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers ;;
esac
sync_helper=$helper_dir/sync-instance-upgrade
case "$self" in
    */deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/restore-chatbot-root)
        sync_helper=$helper_dir/../../scripts/sync-instance-upgrade.sh ;;
esac
sync_helper=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_SYNC_INSTANCE_UPGRADE_HELPER:-$sync_helper}") || fail 'selected sync helper absent'
secure_path "$sync_helper"
[ -f "$sync_helper" ] && [ -x "$sync_helper" ] || fail 'selected sync helper not executable'
if [ "$state" = Running ]; then
    # A service restart observes only; it must not replace a running guest's lowers.
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FSTYPE)" = overlay ] || fail 'running root is not overlay'
    options=$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FS-OPTIONS) || fail 'cannot inspect running root'
    case ",$options," in *,"lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer",*) ;; *) fail 'running root lower pins differ' ;; esac
    case ",$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o VFS-OPTIONS)," in *,ro,*) ;; *) fail 'running root is not read-only' ;; esac
    exit 0
fi
[ "$check_only" != true ] || exit 0
exec "$sync_helper" boot "$name"

# The name selects the native target; the same existing UUID/session/key and

seed_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/seed-layer
upgrade_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade-layer
readback() { timeout --kill-after=5s 30s "$@"; }
secure_path() (
    path=$1
    [ "$(realpath -e -- "$path")" = "$path" ] || fail "noncanonical path: $path"
    while :; do
        [ ! -L "$path" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u -- "$path")" = 0 ] &&
            [ $((0$(stat -c %a -- "$path") & 022)) -eq 0 ] || fail "unsafe owner/mode: $path"
        [ "$path" != / ] || break
        path=$(dirname -- "$path")
    done
)
secure_path "$pool"
[ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$pool")" = 0:0 ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&

    .root_bound==true and .root_view_readonly==true and .upgrade_paired==true and
    .threetched_root==$root and .root_view==$view and .instance.name==$name and .instance.type=="container" and

    .config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid and .config["user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key"]==$key and

helper_dir=$(dirname -- "$self")
case "$helper_dir" in
    /usr/local/libexec/3tched)
        helper_dir=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers ;;
esac
sync_helper=$helper_dir/sync-instance-upgrade
case "$self" in
    */deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/restore-chatbot-root)
        sync_helper=$helper_dir/../../scripts/sync-instance-upgrade.sh ;;
esac
sync_helper=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_SYNC_INSTANCE_UPGRADE_HELPER:-$sync_helper}") || fail 'selected sync helper absent'
secure_path "$sync_helper"
[ -f "$sync_helper" ] && [ -x "$sync_helper" ] || fail 'selected sync helper not executable'

    exit 0
fi
[ "$check_only" != true ] || exit 0
exec "$sync_helper" boot "$name"

```sh
helper=/usr/local/libexec/3tched/op-identity-root
gpt=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool/.provisioning/3tchedChatbot.boot.json
if [ -e "$gpt" ] || [ -L "$gpt" ]; then
    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/restore-chatbot-root || exit 1
    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/runit-ready-signal identity-roots
    exec sleep infinity
```

physical=${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_STATE:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/seed-identities}
legacy=${IDENTITIES:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/identities}
physical_present=0
seed_readonly_ready=0
failed=0
for receipt in "$physical"/*/state.json; do
    [ -e "$receipt" ] || [ -L "$receipt" ] || continue
    physical_present=1
    name=$(basename "$(dirname "$receipt")")
    if [ "$name" != 3tchedChatbot ] && ! printf '%s' "$name" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
        echo "physical seed staging receipt $name: boot disabled"
        continue
    fi
    marker="$physical/$name/boot-ready.json"
    if [ ! -e "$marker" ] && [ ! -L "$marker" ]; then
        echo "physical seed $name: no authoritative-completion boot opt-in; skipped"
        continue
    fi
    # A canonical name alone does not prove provisioning completed. The helper
    # checks the owner attestation marker and all storage/native identity pins.
    if ! jq -e --arg name "$name" '
        .name == $name and .phase == "ready" and
        (.session == $name or ($name == "3tchedChatbot" and .session == "b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28"))
    ' "$receipt" >/dev/null; then
        echo "physical seed $name: invalid/incomplete receipt; legacy suppressed" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        continue
    fi
    start_on_boot=$(jq -er '.start_on_boot | select(type == "boolean") | tostring' "$marker") || {
        echo "physical seed $name: invalid boot completion policy" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        continue
    }
    # The physical partition's kernel RO flag is volatile across reboot.
    # The host owner restores it once, after ready/opt-in selection and before
    # any seed-check/up; verification failures stop boot restoration closed.
    if [ "$seed_readonly_ready" -eq 0 ]; then
        "$helper" seed-readonly || { echo "physical seed read-only enforcement failed" >&2; exit 1; }
        seed_readonly_ready=1
    fi
    state=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name/state" | jq -er '.status') || state=unknown
    case "$state" in
        Running)
            if "$helper" seed-check "$name"; then
                "$helper" seed-lungs "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;
        Stopped)
            if "$helper" seed-up "$name" && "$helper" seed-lungs "$name"; then
                if [ "$start_on_boot" = true ]; then incus start "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
                else echo "physical seed $name: storage restored; boot start disabled"; fi
            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;
        *) echo "physical seed $name: unsupported native status $state" >&2
            failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
    esac
done
if [ "$physical_present" -eq 1 ]; then
    # A direct legacy lower mount conflicts with sprouts from the SAME seed,
    # even for a different identity. Do not invoke legacy `up` in this mode.
    for image in "$legacy"/*/identity.img; do
        [ -f "$image" ] || continue
        name=$(basename "$(dirname "$image")")
        if [ -e "$physical/$name/state.json" ] || [ -L "$physical/$name/state.json" ]; then
            echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by physical seed receipt"
        else
            echo "legacy identity $name: migration or independent lower required; shared seed direct mount suppressed" >&2
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        fi
    done
else
    "$helper" up || failed=$((failed + 1))
    "$helper" status || failed=$((failed + 1))
fi
[ "$failed" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$failed identity root startup check(s) failed" >&2; exit 1; }

# An absent pool must not hide GPT receipts and select the legacy root path.
secure_path "$pool" || exit 1
[ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$pool")" = 0:0 ] &&
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o UUID)" = a1ab7b42-12a8-437c-8f65-d0469892c8dd ] &&
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M / -o UUID)" != a1ab7b42-12a8-437c-8f65-d0469892c8dd ] ||
    fail 'canonical loop pool is not mounted on its pinned filesystem'
if [ -e "$pool/.provisioning" ] || [ -L "$pool/.provisioning" ]; then
    secure_path "$pool/.provisioning" || exit 1
    [ -d "$pool/.provisioning" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$pool/.provisioning")" = 0:0:700 ] ||
        fail 'preparation receipt directory must be private'
fi
physical=${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_STATE:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/seed-identities}
legacy=${IDENTITIES:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/identities}
gpt_present=0
gpt_name=
physical_present=0
physical_names=
selected_sessions='|'
# GPT boot receipts attest completed adoption; restore --check verifies exact
# native UUID/session/key plus the corresponding private disk/root receipts.
# Restoration needs no online preparation replay, regardless of native name.
# Never execute restoration while another receipt could name the same chatbot.
for receipt in "$pool"/.provisioning/*.boot.json; do
    [ -e "$receipt" ] || [ -L "$receipt" ] || continue
    gpt_present=1
    private_receipt "$receipt" || fail "unsafe GPT boot receipt: $receipt"
    name=$(basename "$receipt" .boot.json)
    [ -z "$gpt_name" ] || fail 'multiple GPT chatbot boot receipts; reconcile before restoration'
    "$restore_helper" --check "$name" || fail "invalid GPT chatbot boot receipt: $name"
    gpt_name=$name
    selected_sessions="$selected_sessions$chatbot_session|"
done
for receipt in "$physical"/*/state.json; do
    [ -e "$receipt" ] || [ -L "$receipt" ] || continue
    physical_present=1
    name=$(basename "$(dirname "$receipt")")
    marker=$physical/$name/boot-ready.json
    if [ ! -e "$marker" ] && [ ! -L "$marker" ]; then
        echo "physical seed $name: no authoritative-completion boot opt-in; skipped"
        continue
    fi
    private_receipt "$receipt" && private_receipt "$marker" || fail "unsafe physical boot receipts: $name"
    # Keep existing canonical UUID roots. Both chatbot name forms require the
    # same pinned session and complete boot/storage receipt; neither grants identity.
    jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$chatbot_session" '
        .version==1 and .layout=="shared-partition-siblings-v2" and .name==$name and .phase=="ready" and
        (.session|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$")) and
        (.instance_uuid|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$")) and
        (.session==$name or (.session==$sid and
            ($name|test("^(3tchedCtlChatbot|3tchedChatbot|ID-[1-9][0-9]*)$") and length<=63)))
    ' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail "invalid/incomplete physical boot receipt: $name"
    policy=$(jq -er '.start_on_boot|select(type=="boolean")|tostring' "$marker") || fail "invalid physical boot policy: $name"
    expected=$(jq -cS --argjson start "$policy" '{version,layout,image,members,persist,name,session,instance_uuid,root,seed_fsid,seed_generation,sprout_fsid,leaf,leaf_inode,leaf_size,start_on_boot:$start}' "$receipt") || fail "invalid storage pins: $name"
    actual=$(jq -cS . "$marker") || fail "invalid boot marker: $name"
    [ "$expected" = "$actual" ] || fail "physical boot/storage pins differ: $name"
    session=$(jq -er .session "$receipt") || fail "missing physical session: $name"
    case "$selected_sessions" in
        *"|$session|"*) fail "conflicting boot receipts for logical identity $session; no roots restored" ;;
    esac
    selected_sessions="$selected_sessions$session|"
    physical_names="$physical_names $name"
done
failed=0
if [ -n "$gpt_name" ]; then
    "$restore_helper" "$gpt_name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
fi
seed_readonly_ready=0
for name in $physical_names; do
    receipt=$physical/$name/state.json
    marker=$physical/$name/boot-ready.json
    start_on_boot=$(jq -er '.start_on_boot|select(type=="boolean")|tostring' "$marker") || fail "invalid boot policy: $name"
    # The helper checks the complete boot/storage marker, native UUID and
    # session/key binding again under its lifecycle lock before touching roots.
    if [ "$seed_readonly_ready" -eq 0 ]; then
        "$helper" seed-readonly || fail 'physical seed read-only enforcement failed'
        seed_readonly_ready=1
    fi
    state=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name/state" | jq -er '.status') || state=unknown
    case "$state" in
        Running)
            if "$helper" seed-check "$name"; then
                "$helper" seed-lungs "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;
        Stopped)
            if "$helper" seed-up "$name" && "$helper" seed-lungs "$name"; then
                if [ "$start_on_boot" = true ]; then incus start "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
                else echo "physical seed $name: storage restored; boot start disabled"; fi
            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;
        *) echo "physical seed $name: unsupported native status $state" >&2
            failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
    esac
done
if [ "$physical_present" -eq 1 ] || [ "$gpt_present" -eq 1 ]; then
    # Never select legacy `up`: directly mounting the same seed conflicts with
    # retained sprouts even when another identity's root failed restoration.
    for image in "$legacy"/*/identity.img; do
        [ -f "$image" ] || continue
        name=$(basename "$(dirname "$image")")
        case "$selected_sessions" in
            *"|$name|"*) echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by selected boot receipt"; continue ;;
        esac
        if { [ "$name" = 3tchedChatbot ] || [ "$name" = 3tchedCtlChatbot ]; } && [ "$gpt_present" -eq 1 ]; then
            echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by GPT boot receipt"
        elif [ -e "$physical/$name/state.json" ] || [ -L "$physical/$name/state.json" ]; then
            echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by physical seed receipt"
        else
            echo "legacy identity $name: migration or independent lower required; shared seed direct mount suppressed" >&2
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        fi
    done
else
    "$helper" up || failed=$((failed + 1))
    "$helper" status || failed=$((failed + 1))
fi
[ "$failed" -eq 0 ] || fail "$failed identity root startup check(s) failed"
"$helper_dir/runit-ready-signal" identity-roots || exit 1
exec sleep infinity
